mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS increase, or IC > 0.05 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 50,000 jobs in the prior month signals labor market strength that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns upward over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 50,000 by more than 10,000 jobs in the prior month
failure_condition: Forward returns underperform a 5-day moving average baseline with p < 0.05, or unemployment rate falls sharply in the following 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) accompanied by a drop in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates an economic contraction that elevates risk premia and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: both HOUST and INDPRO fall by at least 10% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day cumulative forward return exceeds zero despite the contraction, or IC < 0.1 over the 5-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 2% monthly for two consecutive months suggests supply-side expansion that outpaces demand, pushing up valuations and lowering S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly growth rate exceeds 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Forward returns beat a 5-day risk-free benchmark with p < 0.05, or INDPRO decelerates in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, it indicates a labor market shift that lowers real interest rates, encouraging equity accumulation and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative, or IC > 0.05 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 suggests weakening labor demand, raising perceived risk and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by 150,000 in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive with p < 0.05, or unemployment rate falls sharply in the next month.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both consumer confidence proxies (HOUST) and retail sales (not available in evidence - so skip this one) would indicate weakening demand, but since we can't use unavailable series, instead use a decline in RSAFS (retail sales proxy) and HOUST together to signal weakness, predicting negative 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: both HOUST and RSAFS fall by 5% or more in the prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is positive with IC > 0.2, or either series recovers sharply in the following days.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle regime (as signaled by FEDFUNDS), S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days tend to be negative due to higher discount rates, regardless of other macro variables.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of tightening cycles (rolling IC < -0.2).
